'''Casey Gardner Jacobsen''' (born March 19, 1981) is an American retired professional [[basketball]] player who played four seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also had an extensive European basketball career, mostly while playing with [[Brose Baskets Bamberg]], in Germany. With Brose, he won the [[List of German basketball champions|Bundesliga championship]] in 2007 and 2010, while also receiving the [[Basketball Bundesliga Finals MVP|German League Finals MVP]] award. He won Bundesliga championships in 2011, 2012, and 2013. He also won the [[German Basketball Cup|German Cup]] with Bamberg, in 2010, 2011, and 2012, and the [[German Basketball Supercup|German Supercup]] four times (2007, 2010, 2011, 2012).{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} Following his retirement in 2014, Brose Baskets retired his jersey number 23.

==High school==
Jacobsen attended [[Glendora High School]], in [[Glendora, California]], where he played high school basketball.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Player Bio: Casey Jacobsen|url=https://gostanford.com/news/2013/4/17/208433537.aspx|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Stanford University Athletics|language=en}}</ref> He was a [[McDonald's All-American]] selection.<ref>{{Cite web|title=1999 McDonalds All-American Rosters – High School Basketball – RealGM|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/highschool/mcdonalds/Rosters/1999|access-date=2021-02-22|website=Basketball.realgm.com}}</ref>

==College career==
After high school, Jacobsen played [[NCAA Division I]] [[college basketball]] at [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford University]], where he scored a career-high of 49 points against [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State University]], on January 31, 2002.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-feb-01-sp-pacten01-story.html|title=Jacobsen Scores 49 for Stanford|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=February 1, 2002|access-date=December 20, 2022}}</ref> He was a First Team [[All-American]] his sophomore year, and a Second Team All-American his junior year. Jacobsen was also a three-time [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] selection. In his three years in college with Stanford, he finished third in points scored (1,723), sixth in points per game (18.1), second in three-point goals (222), and fourth in three-point percentage (.427) in the school's history.

==Professional career==
After his career at [[Stanford University]], Jacobsen was the 22nd overall pick in the [[2002 NBA draft]], selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He was later traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for [[Jim Jackson (basketball)|Jim Jackson]]. Jacobsen averaged 5.2 points per game through his career and is known as a player with exceptional range on his shot, out to beyond the [[NBA]] three-point line. His usual positions are [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Casey Jacobsen Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jacobca01.html|access-date=2021-02-22|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref>

After playing for [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Vitoria]] of the [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|Spanish ACB League]] during the 2005–06 season, he signed a non-guaranteed contract with the [[Houston Rockets]], and played in four preseason games with them, but was released on October 27, 2006, before the 2006–07 season began.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2006-10-27-notes_x.htm|title=NBA notes: Fortson suspended; Shinn selling New Orleans home |website=Usatoday30.usatoday.com|access-date=13 December 2021}}</ref> Jacobsen then moved to the [[Brose Baskets]] (Bamberg, Germany) of the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German League]], where he won the German Basketball Championship in 2007, and he also earned [[Basketball Bundesliga Finals MVP|the Finals MVP Award]].

Jacobsen returned to the NBA when he was signed by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on July 24, 2007, and he spent the 2007–08 season with them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportsline.com/nba/story/10267561|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080715151259/http://www.sportsline.com/nba/story/10267561|url-status=dead|title=Jacobsen signs with Memphis after two seasons in Europe|archive-date=15 July 2008|access-date=13 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news|title=News|website=Nba.com|access-date=13 December 2021}}</ref>

On July 1, 2008, the Grizzlies chose not to offer Jacobsen a new contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/jul/01/griz-to-go-slow-in-free-agency|title=Griz to go slow in free agency|website=Commercialappeal.com|access-date=13 December 2021}}</ref> Jacobsen's final NBA game was on April 16, 2008, in a 111–120 loss to the [[ Denver Nuggets ]] where he recorded 8 points, 7 assists and 5 rebounds.

In August 2008, he signed with the German League club [[ALBA Berlin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/item/34657|title=Alba completes roster with Jacobsen|website=Euroleague.net|access-date=13 December 2021}}</ref>

In June 2009 Jacobsen signed a new contract with his former team [[Brose Baskets Bamberg]] in Germany. He led his team to win both the German Cup (Pokalsieger) <ref>{{Cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date=11 April 2010|title=German Cup Final Four:April 10–11, 2010|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/uleb/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2009-2010/germany/i/70086/3864/german-cup-final-four-april-10-11-2010|url-status=dead|department=News|language=en|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111127041359/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/uleb/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2009-2010/germany/i/70086/3864/german-cup-final-four-april-10-11-2010|archive-date=27 November 2011}}</ref> and German Championship <ref>{{Cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date=17 June 2010|title=German League finals, Game 5: June 17, 2010|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/uleb/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2009-2010/germany/i/72663/3864/german-league-finals-game-5-june-17-2010|url-status=dead|department=News|language=en|publisher=EuroLeague|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730191215/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/uleb/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2009-2010/germany/i/72663/3864/german-league-finals-game-5-june-17-2010|archive-date=30 July 2012}}</ref> in 2010 and was again named Finals MVP.<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/VG0XmZ3-ngw Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20160610023108/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VG0XmZ3-ngw Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VG0XmZ3-ngw| title = MVP Finals 2010 – Casey Jacobsen | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Jacobsen re-signed with Brose Baskets Bamberg in August 2010 for the 2010–2011 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2010-11-signings/i/74784/4465/brose-baskets-re-signs-jacobsen-adds-hines |title=BROSE BASKETS re-signs Jacobsen, adds Hines – 2010–11 SIGNINGS – Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL |access-date=2011-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720154254/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2010-11-signings/i/74784/4465/brose-baskets-re-signs-jacobsen-adds-hines |archive-date=2012-07-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The team again won the German Cup in April 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.beko-bbl.de/magazin/artikel.php?artikel%3D25337%26menuid%3D1064 |title=Beko Basketball Bundesliga – Deutscher Pokalsieger 2011: Brose Baskets |access-date=2011-04-15 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315055839/http://www.beko-bbl.de/magazin/artikel.php?artikel=25337&menuid=1064 |archive-date=2012-03-15 }}</ref> At game five of the finals he announced that he extended his contract for three more years. During this time, he won the German Championships in the years 2012 and 2013 and also the German Cup in 2012. In May 2014, Jacobsen, along with his longtime teammate [[John Goldsberry]], announced retirement from professional basketball. In tribute to him, Brose Baskets retired his 23 jersey number.<ref>{{cite web|title=GOODBYE, JOHN & CASEY!|url=http://www.brosebaskets.de/saison/news/artikel/goodbye-john-casey/|work=brosebaskets.de|access-date=23 May 2014|language=de|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140528035806/http://www.brosebaskets.de/saison/news/artikel/goodbye-john-casey/|archive-date=28 May 2014}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
After retiring from playing basketball, it was announced by the [[Phoenix Suns]] that Jacobsen would not only be a broadcaster during some pre-game and post-game shows with [[Tom Chambers (basketball)|Tom Chambers]], but he would also hold his own show under the Rise Suns Digital Network.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/media-day-2014|title = Media Day 2014|website = [[NBA.com]]}}</ref> He would make his debut as a broadcaster on the November 2014 game against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In addition, Jacobsen would also take on the college basketball analyst role for [[Fox Sports]] and the Pac-12 Networks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/10/08/phoenix-suns-jazz-reunite-3-german-league-teammates/73616942/|title=Phoenix Suns, Jazz reunite 3 German League teammates|first=Paul|last=Coro|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|access-date=13 December 2021}}</ref>
